_evidence: 0x0053dc57 (compose after menu_0084300a, globals=layout only so the static links and handlers keep their image values): esi = [[0x82fd34]] with no null test of the header (callers only run with a current menu), then for each item until the null link: cmp dl=[0x82fd45], item id +0xc (je skips the handler), else 'call [item+0x1a]' with esi = item, edx = 1, ebx = [item+0xe], ah = +0x1f, cx = the entry's word +0x20, and 'cmp ah,[item+0x1f]; jne' marks the item when the handler changed +0x1f; otherwise byte [0x81e4fb] == 0xff marks it, else +0x1e bit 0x20 with (word +0x20 & cx) does. The current menu is the static 13-item menu 0x84300a, whose items carry the real handlers 0x538e1a (items 1-5, value at 0x81e4f8) and 0x52c43d (items 6-13, value at 0x7ab544): with edx = 1 both only clear bit 7 of +0x1f and set it again when the item's value (type +0xd: byte/word/dword; 3 = the empty stub 0x54e232) equals [ebx] (0x5398c4), so +0x1f changes in some cases and not in others and nothing faults. Items 1-5 have +0x1e bit 0x20 clear and items 6-13 set with word +0x20 = 0xf000, so both outcomes of the mask test occur with the random entry word. The selection [0x82fd45] takes every id 1..13 (handler skipped) and 0/0xff (no match); [0x81e4fb] is 0xff about half the time (its dword 0x81e4f8 is varied by menu_0084300a, this byte overrides its top byte). Item byte +0x1e (0x843040+0x1e and the real item strides) is varied too, mixing bit 0x20 (the mask test), 0x80 (0x538e1a skips its value compare) and 0x40, starting from the image values 0xc0/0xc2/0x60/0x61.
